parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the spring constant k of a spring by two methods. Some of the apparatus has been set up for you. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1 and Fig. 1.2. Method 1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Measure the unstretched length l 0 of the spring, in mm. l 0 = ....................................................mm [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Hang the 300 g mass on the spring, as shown in Fig. 1.1.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Use the equation e = ( l – l 0 ) to calculate the extension e of the spring. e = ....................................................mm [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate a value for the spring constant k using the equation k e F = , where F = 3.0 N. k = ............................................... N / mm [1] Method 2

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Adjust the position of the lower clamp so that the pin is level with the bottom of the mass when the mass is not moving. Pull the mass down about 1.5 cm and release it so that it oscillates up and down. Fig. 1.2 shows one complete oscillation.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Measure the time t taken for 10 complete oscillations. Start the stopwatch as the bottom of the mass passes the pin. t = ........................................................s [1]
